1.	Christoph Henkel was the vice chairman of Henkel AG's shareholders' committee and is founding partner of investment firm Canyon Equity.
2.	With brands like Persil, Schwarzkopf, and Fa, and over $24 billion in annual revenue, Henkel AG is one of the world's biggest cleaning products companies.
3.	After the death of his father Konrad in 1999, Christoph Henkel inherited part of his interests and became the largest single stockholder in the company.
4.	He is founding partner of Canyon Equity LLC; a private-equity firm in California that has acquired or developed luxury resorts in Fiji, Utah, Wyoming and New Mexico.
5.	He also invests in real estate in Europe as well as in tech, biotech and movie-production companies.

Did you know?
1.	In the 1990s, Henkel cofounded Los Angeles-based production company Cineville; it has produced more than 55 feature films over the years.

2.	Active in acquiring land for conservation, he is married to the German art dealer and collector Katrin Bellinger; the couple have an extensive private art collection.


Quote
"We were taught from early childhood that the family business comes before the family."

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Christopher Zeller controls Ivoclar Vivadent, a closely-held maker of dental products and systems based in Schaan, Principality of Liechtenstein.","ounded in 1923 focusing on the production of artificial teeth, the company was bought by Zeller's grandfather, Dr. Adolf Schneider, in 1948.","Zeller served as CEO from 1990 to 2003. He served on the company's supervisory board until 2025, after having stepped down as chairman in 2019.","Today, Ivoclar Vivadent has subsidiaries in more than 50 countries, employs around 3,600 people and generates annual revenue in excess of $900 million."]
abouts: ["Zeller's wife, Christina, also serves on the supervisory board."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Christopher \"Kit\" Goldsbury's fortune comes from selling salsa maker Pace Foods to Campbell Soup for $1.1 billion in 1994.","Goldsbury worked on the assembly line at Pace in 1969, two years after marrying founder David Pace's daughter Linda. He became president in 1977.","After Goldsbury and Linda separated in 1987, Goldsbury purchased her half for $95 million, a fraction of what he sold it for seven years later.","The San Antonio billionaire is backing the revitalization of the downtown Pearl neighborhood through his private equity firm Silver Ventures."]
title: Chief Executive Officer

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Activist investor Chris Hohn founded The Children's Investment Fund, a London-based hedge fund, in 2003.","The fund now manages $77 billion and has large, concentrated positions in a handful of stocks, including Microsoft, Visa and GE Aerospace.","Hohn donates a portion of the firm's earnings to his Children's Investment Fund Foundation, which has an endowment exceeding $6 billion.","The son of a Jamaican car mechanic, Hohn attended Southampton University in the U.K. and got an MBA at Harvard.","He briefly worked in consulting and private equity, before joining Richard Perry's hedge fund, Perry Capital, in 1996."]
abouts: ["Hohn paid his ex-wife, Jamie Cooper, over $500 million in a divorce settlement in 2014,  reportedly the largest ever in U.K. history at the time.","Hohn has steered over $2 billion to charity, earning himself knighthood in 2014."]
title: Founder

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Christopher Kwok is the younger son of property mogul Raymond Kwok, chairman of Sun Hung Kai Properties, one of the largest developers in Hong Kong.","He's served as an executive director at Sun Hung Kai since 2016, taking charge of sales, project management and the leasing of major projects.","He's also a member of the Beijing Municipal Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference.","In 2012, his father and his uncle Thomas became involved in a bribery investigation. Raymond was acquitted but Thomas was found guilty and sentenced to five years in prison in 2014."]
abouts: ["Christopher's brother, Edward, and three of his cousins are also billionaires.","Christopher and his wife, Rachel Zhao, a former news anchor for China's Phoenix TV, met while they studied at Stanford University in 2013."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Christopher MacMillan is one of 21 billionaire heirs to Cargill, the world's biggest agriculture business.","His great-great-grandfather, W.W. Cargill, founded the business as a single grain warehouse on the end of an Iowa railroad line in 1865.","The family still owns roughly 90% of Cargill, which did $154 billion in 2025 sales across food, agriculture, financial and industrial divisions.","He's one of nine billionaire siblings who inherited stakes in the company from their father John H.  MacMillan III, who died in 2008."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Chris Olah is cofounder and interpretability research lead at Anthropic, which builds large-scale artificial intelligence systems. ","He cofounded Anthropic in 2021 with six other ex-OpenAI employees. ","Anthropic, which private investors valued $965 billion in May 2026, has partnerships with Google's parent company Alphabet and Amazon. ","Olah previously worked in a similar role at OpenAI and was a researcher at Google Brain. ","Olah skipped college and was named a Thiel Fellow in 2012, when he was 19. In 2020, he wrote a blog post to help others decide if they should follow a similar path."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Chris Rokos is the founder of hedge fund firm Rokos Capital Management.","Rokos is a macro investor who trades currencies, interest rates and commodities, as well as equities.","Rokos founded his London-based firm in 2015 and it now manages some $12 billion and employs more than 200 people.","A founding partner of Brevan Howard Asset Management, Rokos left the hedge fund firm after having a falling out with his partner, Alan Howard."]
title: CEO & Founder

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Christopher Stolte cofounded data analytics company Tableau in 2003.","Salesforce acquired Tableau in June 2019 in a $15.7 billion, all-stock deal.","Stolte left Tableau that year and now runs his family foundation?which focuses on climate, education and civic engagement causes.","Tableau was born out of Stolte's Stanford thesis, analyzing and visualizing databases under his then-advisor, later-cofounder Pat Hanrahan.","He and his cofounders raised just $15 million in venture capital before taking Tableau public in May 2013."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Christy Walton married into what is now the richest family in the world: Walmart's Walton clan.","She inherited a stake in the retailer when her husband, John Walton, died in a 2005 plane crash.","Christy received about one sixth of her husband's estate; her son, Lukas Walton, got about one third.","She was one of the biggest backers of the Lincoln Project, an anti-Trump super-PAC that ran ads in battleground states during the 2020 campaign.","She leads a very private life in Jackson, Wyoming."]
abouts: ["Her son, Lukas, battled cancer as a child. She reportedly claimed that an all-organic diet eliminated his tumor.","In 2010, she established Cuna del Mar, an investment fund that backs companies working to develop a sustainable supply of seafood."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Chu Jian founded automation products supplier Zhejiang Supcon Technology in 1999.","Chu received his doctorate in engineering from Zhejiang University in 1989.","Supcon is headquartered in the eastern Chinese city of Hangzhou."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Chu Lam Yiu is co-chairman of fragrances and tobacco flavoring supplier Huabao International Holdings.","She founded the company in 1996 and took it public on Hong Kong through a \"backdoor listing\" a decade later.","Chu's son Lam Ka Yu became co-chairman in June 2021."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Chu Mang Yee is a former government official who controls Hong Kong-listed real estate developer Hopson Development.","Chu's daughter, Chu Kut Yung, is the company's chairman.","Over his business career, Chu has built experience in trading and construction as well as real estate development.","Founded in 1992, Hopson focused on mid- and high-end residential projects.","Over his business career, Chu has build experience in trading and construction as well as real estate development.","Kut Yung is a graduate of Renmin University with a finance degree."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["High school dropout Chua Thian Poh got his start making hooks and spikes for the logging industry.","In 1987 Chua founded luxury property developer Ho Bee Land, known for building high-end condos in Sentosa, Singapore's island resort.","The company has a diversified portfolio that includes commercial property overseas, notably in London and Munich.","Since 2020 it has bought five sites in suburban Australia where it plans to build master-planned residential communities.","In 2022, Ho Bee acquired the Scalpel office tower in London's financial district for $961 million."]
abouts: ["Chua was once Singapore's non-resident ambassador to the Republic of Maldives.","He's set up a family office called One Hill Capital.\r\n","In 2018, Ho Bee purchased a London office block for $850 million.","His son, Nicholas, is Ho Bee Land's CEO."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Chung Mong-joon is the largest shareholder of shipbuilder Hyundai Heavy Industries.","He is the sixth son of the late Hyundai group founder Chung Ju-yung, who got his start repairing trucks for the U.S. Army after the Korean War.","Chung ran Hyundai Heavy Industries until he entered politics in 1988; he served seven terms in the National Assembly."]
abouts: ["In 2014, he ran for mayor of Seoul but lost.","He is a former vice president of international soccer body FIFA."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Chung Yong-ji is the founder and CEO of South Korean biotechnology company Caregen, best known for its anti-wrinkle treatment and diabetes drugs. ","U.S.-educated Chung founded Caregen in 2001 and listed on Korea's technology-rich Kosdaq stock exchange in 2015.","Caregen sells its products to more than 130 countries, and its biggest markets are in the Middle East and North Africa, Europe and Asia Pacific regions.","The company's other major revenue source is another injectable product called Dr. CYJ Hair Filler, that claims to help regrow hair. "]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Chung Yong-jin is a grandson of Samsung group founder Lee Byung-Chull and a cousin of Samsung Electronics executive chairman Jay Y. Lee.","The bulk of his fortune comes from Samsung Electronics and discount chain E-Mart, a unit of Korea's retail conglomerate Shinsegae Group.","In 2024, Chung was promoted from vice chairman to chairman of Shinsegae, a retail conglomerate.","In 2021, Shinsegae acquired Korean baseball team SK Wyverns (now SSG Landers), winner of four championships, from the SK group for about $120 million."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Claire Bristow is one of four sisters of Frank Holding, Chairman and CEO of First Citizens Bank, a $31 billion (market cap) commercial banking chain, since 2008.","Bristow's grandfather, Robert Powell Holding, became an employee of the bank in 1918, and became president by 1935, before passing it down to Frank's father, Lewis Holding.","Today, Bristow, her three sisters, and her brother Frank collectively own about 20% of the bank."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Clark Hunt is chairman and CEO of the NFL's Kansas City Chiefs, which he owns with his three siblings.","Their father Lamar Hunt (d. 2006) founded the team and passed control to his kids in 2005. Lamar is credited with naming the Super Bowl.","Forbes estimates the Chiefs are now worth more than $4.7 billion (net of debt). Each Hunt Sibling owns an estimated 25% stake.","The Hunt siblings also own MLS team FC Dallas and a minority stake in the NBA's Chicago Bulls. Clark is chairman and CEO of the family's soccer club, while brother Dan is president.","Lamar was one of 11 heirs of oil wildcatter H.L. Hunt (d. 1974) who appeared on the first ever Forbes 400 list of the richest Americans in 1982."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Claudio Del Vecchio is one of six children of Leonardo Del Vecchio, the late chairman (d. 2022) of EssilorLuxottica, the world's largest eyeglasses firm.","He inherited a 12.5% stake in his father's Luxembourg-based holding company Delfin after his death, along with his stepmother and six siblings.","Besides EssilorLuxottica, Delfin also owns shares in insurer Generali; banks Monte dei Paschi di Siena and UniCredit; and real estate developer Covivio.","Claudio served as Luxottica's co-CEO in the 1990s and took the company public on the New York Stock Exchange in 1990.","He acquired Brooks Brothers, America's oldest clothing retailer, in 2001; the firm filed for bankruptcy in September 2020."]
abouts: ["Claudio moved from Italy to New York in 1982 and helped spearhead Luxottica's entry into the U.S. market in the 1980s.","He was awarded the title of Cavaliere del Lavoro, one of Italy's highest civilian honors, in 2014."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Clay Bavor is a cofounder of Sierra, an AI startup that makes customer service agents.","Before Sierra, Bavor spent 18 years at Google, where he lead the company's emerging tech efforts in virtual and augmented reality.","Bavor and Sierra cofounder Bret Taylor met a Google, where they were hired by Marissa Mayer, who would go on to become CEO of Yahoo.","In September, Sierra raised $350 million, led by Greenoaks Capital, valuing the startup at $10 billion."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Clayton Zekelman owns a stake in his family's steel business, Zekelman Industries.","The $3.3 billion (revenues) company is one of North America's largest steel pipe and tube makers.","The company has also pumped more than $1 billion into Z Modular, a division that is developing modular apartment complexes in places such as Texas, Arizona and Canada.","Clayton and his brothers, fellow billionaires Barry Zekelman and Alan Zekelman, split 100% ownership of Zekelman Industries.","They sold the company to the Carlyle Group in 2006 for some $1.2 billion, but bought the business back in 2011."]
abouts: ["One of Zekelman Industries' subsidiaries, Atlas Tube, produced steel for stretches of the Mexican border wall in Arizona."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Clelia Haji-Ioannou is the daughter of Loucas Haji-Ioannou, the late Greek Cypriot shipping magnate (d. 2008).","She is a billionaire thanks to her stake in discount airline easyJet, founded by her brother Stelios.","She owns real estate across Europe, including properties in Monaco and Greece.","She also has a gallery outside of Athens featuring artwork by Picasso, Warhol and Dali."]
abouts: ["Haji-Ioannou oversaw the publication of a biography of her father, \"Loucas Haji-Ioannou: The King of the Tankers.\"","Born in Athens, Clelia Haji-Ioannou holds both Cypriot and British citizenship and sits on the board of the Cyprus Marine Environment Protection Association."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Clemens Fischer is serial pharmaceutical and supplement entrepreneur who owns the Futrue Group, a Munich-based holding company with a collection of about 20 drug and R&D companies.","Over the last two decades, he has built and sold a series of companies in the over-the-counter drug and supplement space, from sleep aids to irritable bowel syndrome treatments.","Fischer's newest company is Vertanical, the Munich-based pharmaceutical company developing a cannabinoid-based extract to treat chronic pain.","Vertanical is pursuing approval for its drug Ver-01 in the European Union and eventually in the United States with hopes for it to become the first cannabis-based prescription painkiller.","Born in Weilheim, Germany, Fischer became a medical doctor but stopped practicing medicine decades ago to get an MBA from Harvard and become an entrepreneur."]
bio: Clemens Fischer is a serial pharmaceutical and supplement entrepreneur who is on a mission to create the first cannabis-based pharmaceutical medication to treat chronic pain. His Munich-based pharmaceutical company Vertanical hopes to disrupt the $20 billion (annual sales) opioid market with its botanical drug, which has been shown to have less side effects in studies than opioid-based painkillers.

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Clemens Toennies owns 45% of German food industry giant Toennies Lebensmittel, with annual revenue of around $6 billion. His son Maximilian owns 5%.","Operating meat, convenience, ingredients and logistics divisions, the company specializes in pig, sow and beef cattle slaughtering and processing.","Clemens attended butchery college and, in 1971, cofounded the company with his brother, Bernd.","Bernd died in 1994, at age 42. His son, Robert, now owns 50% of the business, which employs more than 15,000 people in facilities in Germany and Denmark.","Clemens fought in court with Robert for several years. In 2017, they settled their dispute over ownership of stakes in the company."]
abouts: ["For many years, Clemens presided over pro soccer team FC Schalke 04. He resigned from his post as chairman in June 2020.","Pressure on him had been mounting after racist remarks in 2019, poor team performance on the field, and a Covid-19 outbreak at one of his company's slaughterhouses."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Clemente Del Vecchio is one of six children of Leonardo Del Vecchio, the late chairman (d. 2022) of EssilorLuxottica, the world's largest eyeglasses firm.","He inherited a 12.5% stake in his father's Luxembourg-based holding company Delfin after his death, along with his stepmother and six siblings.","Besides EssilorLuxottica, Delfin also owns shares in insurer Generali; banks Monte dei Paschi di Siena and UniCredit; and real estate developer Covivio.","He is one of two children Del Vecchio had with Sabina Grossi, Luxottica's former head of investor relations, along with his brother Luca.","After inheriting his stake in his father's fortune in 2022, Clemente became the world's youngest billionaire at age 18."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Cliff Obrecht is cofounder and chief operating officer of design software maker Canva, which was valued by private investors at $42 billion in August 2025.","Canva was launched in 2013 by Obrecht, now-wife Melanie Perkins and Cameron Adams in Sydney, Australia, but was met by investor skepticism due to its location.","Like Perkins, Obrecht owns an estimated 18% stake. The couple has pledged to transfer more than 80% of their stake to the Canva Foundation for charitable causes.","Defying the doubts, Canva has attracted 240 million monthly users to its freemium software, with 6 million teams from companies like Zoom paying for it.","Canva's software enables the creation of attractive visuals for menus, resumes and Instagram graphics."]
abouts: ["Obrecht proposed to cofounder Perkins in Turkey's Cappadocia region with a $30 engagement ring."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Cliff Asness is the cofounder, managing partner and chief investment officer of AQR Capital Management, a money management firm with $187 billion in assets under management. ","AQR stands for Applied Quantitative Research. It focuses on factor-based investing, offering products ranging from hedge funds to mutual funds.","The firm is headquartered in Greenwich, Connecticut, with other locations in Bangaluru, Dubai, Hong Kong, London, Munich and Sydney.","A finance Ph.D, Asness is an active researcher and worked in quantitative research for Goldman Sachs before starting AQR in 1998."]
abouts: ["Asness backed lawmakers who supported New York's marriage equality initiative and is a board member of the International Rescue Committee.","Asness was a teaching assistant at the University of Chicago for Nobel laureate Eugene Fama, whose efficient market hypothesis popularized passive investing."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Clive Calder became a billionaire in 2002, when he sold his music company Zomba Group to German mass media corporation Bertlesmann for $2.7 billion.","The crown jewel of his empire was Jive Records, the record label behind many of the first commercially successful hip hop artists.","The South Africa native founded Zomba in London in 1975, then opened an office in New York City in 1978.","Known for shunning the spotlight, Calder now lives in the Cayman Islands with his wife.","He frequently travels to parts of Africa for charity, and his ELMA Philanthropies works on improving childhood education and health on the continent."]
abouts: ["A native of Johannesburg, Calder started out playing in a band at age 18 to support his mother and sister after his father's death.","Calder signed acts like Billy Ocean, Will Smith, R. Kelly, N' Sync (and later, Justin Timberlake), Backstreet Boys and Britney Spears."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["The ebullient resources player and former member of the Australian Parliament, Clive Palmer became a billionaire in 2019.","His fortune soared after a court ordered a flow of iron ore royalties to his company, Mineralogy, to resume.","He started Mineralogy in 1984 and has built a portfolio of iron ore, thermal coal and hydrocarbon assets.","He also owned Queensland Nickel, which operated a nickel-and-cobalt refinery, but the company collapsed in 2016.","Palmer is engaged in litigation with several parties, including Australia's corporate regulator, the Australian Securities and Investments Commission."]
abouts: ["Palmer plans to build and operate a replica of the Titanic, the luxury ocean liner that sank in 1912 on its maiden voyage.","His daughter Emily is a director on Mineralogy's board.","In September 2025, his case against the Australian government related to his proposed iron ore project was dismissed and he was ordered to pay $13 million."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Colin Huang is the founder of PDD Holdings, the Chinese e-commerce company that changed its name from Pinduoduo in 2023.","Huang, who stepped down as chairman of the company in 2021, is still a major shareholder of PDD.","PDD launched budget shopping site Temu in 2022 to compete with Shein, led by fellow Chinese billionaire Sky Xu.","A serial entrepreneur, Huang earlier founded online games company Xinyoudi and e-commerce platform Ouku.com.","Huang, who has a master's in computer science from the University of Wisconsin, interned at Microsoft in both Beijing and Seattle before starting his career at Google in the U.S. in 2004."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Conni Jonsson founded Swedish investment company EQT Partners AB in 1994.","He has been the chairman of the board since 2014.","Jonsson owns nearly 5% of EQT, which listed its shares on the Stockholm stock exchange in 2019.","EQT has roughly $62 billion (52 billion Euro) in assets under management.","EQT primarily invests in private equity, but has also put funds into venture capital, real estate and infrastructure."]
abouts: ["In 2020, Jonsson personally invested in elder care and housing companies after seeing his own mother's needs."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Constantinos Martinos is the owner of Greek shipping firm Thenamaris, which has a fleet of 87 tankers, bulk carriers, container ships and LNG carriers.","He cofounded the company in 1972 with his mother and two brothers. His brothers, Athanasios and Andreas, split off in 1990 and 1998, respectively, leaving him with Thenamaris.","Collectively, Constantinos and his brothers own the largest shipping fleet in Greece, the largest shipowning nation in the world.","Thenamaris is now run by his son, Nikolas. His other son Ioannis runs shipping services firm Signal Group."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Craig Abod is the founder and owner of Carahsoft, a Virginia-based technology company that specializes in IT services for government agencies.","Abod founded Carahsoft in 2004 and has grown the business to revenue of more than $11 billion.","Carahsoft ranked No. 20 on Forbes's 202 l5ist of America's Largest Private Companies."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Wireless pioneer Craig McCaw and his brothers took over their dad's cable-TV business in 1966.","They sold McCaw Cellular to AT&T in 1994 for $12.6 billion in stock.","McCaw, with backing from Bill Gates and Boeing, cofounded Teledesic in 1990 to provide internet access via satellite. It ceased operations in 2002.","He has stayed out of the limelight since stepping down as chairman of telecom operator Clearwire in 2010, two years before it was acquired by Sprint."]
abouts: ["McCaw owns private James Island off the coast of Vancouver."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Cristiano Crippa is the son of Giuseppe Crippa (d. 2025), the late founder of Technoprobe, an Italian manufacturer of probe cards, small devices that test the functionality of microchips.","He cofounded Technoprobe in 1989 alongside his father in his garage and attic, while his father was still working at semiconductor firm ST.","Technoprobe went public on Euronext Milan in 2022; Cristiano owns an 18% stake.","He has served as Technoprobe's chairman of the board since 2017."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Cristina Green and her husband Philip Green own the embattled retail empire Arcadia Group, which fell into bankruptcy during the Covid-19 pandemic.","The business was subsequently forced to sell its best-known brands, including Topshop, Top Man and Dorothy Perkins.","Outside of Arcadia, the Greens own three yachts worth about $140 million and nearly $40 million of real estate that Cristina was found to have bought through offshore firms.","The Greens have been vilified in Britain for their role in letting home retailer BHS collapse, which put pensions for 19,000 workers at risk in 2016."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Cristina Junqueira was 30 years old in 2013 when she cofounded Brazil-based Nubank, now the world's most valuable digital bank.","She ran Brazilian bank Itaú's largest credit card division before leaving the job to start Nubank alongside cofounders David Vélez and Edward Wible.","Junqueira, a trained engineer with an MBA from Northwestern University, serves as Nu Holding's U.S. CEO and the company's Chief Growth Officer.","She first (briefly) became a billionaire when Nubank debuted--as Nu Holdings--on the New York Stock Exchange in December 2021 at a valuation exceeding $50 billion. ","She re-joined the Forbes billionaires list in 2024. "]
abouts: ["Junqueira signed the papers for Nubank's $15 million Series A from her hospital bed while she was in labor with her first child in 2014.","In 2020, she appeared on the cover of Forbes Brazil and became the first woman to be visibly pregnant on the cover of a Brazilian business publication.\t"]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Cui Genliang chairs Hengtong Group, the main investor in Shanghai-listed Hengtong Optic-electric, a maker of optical fiber and optical cables.","Cui's other business interests include real estate and financial investments.","Before joining the company, he was a factory worker for both garment and rubber."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Cui Lixin is the chairman of aluminum smelter Chuangxin Industries Holdings.","He took the Inner Mongolia-based firm public in Hong Kong in November 2025, raising $706 million.","Cui is also the chairman of Shanghai-listed Innovation New Material Technology, an aluminum product maker that counts Foxconn as one of its customers.","The mogul worked for almost two decades at various government-affiliated companies before striking out on his own."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["In 1964 Cynthia Grossman's father, Burton Grossman, founded Grupo Continental, a soft drink producing and distributing company.","Grupo Continental merged with Embotelladoras Arca in 2011 to create Arca Continental, the second-largest Coca-Cola bottler in Latin America.","Along with her brother Bruce, Cynthia owns around 10% of the company shares.","Arca Continental has over 45 plants and 345 distribution centers across America."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Cyrus Madon is the executive vice chair of Brookfield Asset Management, a Toronto-based spinoff of Brookfield Corp. which manages $1 trillion in assets.","Madon joined Brookfield in 1998 and was previously the CEO of its private equity business. He remains its executive chair of private equity.","He began his career working in corporate finance at PricewaterhouseCoopers and initially joined Brookfield as CFO of its real estate brokerage business.","Madon also serves on the board of the C.D. Howe Institute, an influential Canadian think tank."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Son of a horse breeder, Cyrus Poonawalla founded Serum Institute of India in 1966 and built it into the world's largest vaccine maker (by doses).","Headquartered in Pune city, close to Mumbai, Serum produces over 1.5 billion doses annually of a range of vaccines, including for measles, polio and flu.","Under his U.K.-educated son Adar, Serum's CEO, the company invested $800 million at the peak of the pandemic to build a new factory in Pune to make Covid-19 vaccines.","Poonawalla's assets include a majority stake in listed financial services firm Poonawalla Fincorp as well as a stake in The Ritz-Carlton hotel in Pune.","In 2023, his son Adar bought Aberconway House,  a mansion in London's Mayfair, for 138 million pounds."]
abouts: ["Son Adar, featured in Forbes Asia's Heroes of Philanthropy list, is one of the brand ambassadors for the government's 'Clean India' mission.","Poonawalla has an honorary Doctor of Science degree from the University of Oxford, which is constructing the Cyrus Poonawalla Vaccines Research Building.","Serum's Covishield, the vaccine developed by AstraZeneca and Oxford University, was the most widely used in India during the pandemic.","In 2022, Poonawalla was conferred the Padma Bhushan, one of India's highest civilian honors."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Leopoldo del Pino y Calvo Sotelo inherited a stake in Ferrovial S.A., Spain's largest infrastructure construction and management company.","His father, who founded the company in 1952, died in 2008. Leopoldo's three siblings also inherited stakes in Ferrovial.","Leopoldo's brother Rafael del Pino is the chairman and co-CEO of Ferrovial.","Leopoldo, who owns about 4% of Ferrovial, served as a board member of the company until early 2016."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Dagmar Dolby owns about 36% of publicly-traded audio technology firm Dolby Laboratories, which her husband Ray Dolby (d. 2013) founded in 1965.","The company pioneered surround sound technologies used in thousands of films and products, and most recently, in video games and mobile devices.","Her two sons share voting power over some assets. David is a board member at Dolby Labs; his brother, Tom, is a novelist and filmmaker.","Since 2015, she has committed over $160 million to the University of Cambridge, where Ray Dolby earned a Ph.D. in physics.","In September 2018, Dolby donated $20 million to UC San Francisco to establish the Dolby Family Center for Mood Disorders.","She has also supported the Academy Foundation to fund the construction of the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures in Los Angeles."]
abouts: ["Dagmar Dolby graduated from Heidelberg University in her native Germany. She met Ray in 1962 while studying in a summer language program in the U.K.","The Smithsonian National Museum of American History's Ray and Dagmar Dolby Hall of Culture features the ruby slippers worn by Judy Garland in The Wizard of Oz."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Fried chicken billionaire Dan Cathy is chairman of Chick-fil-A, the fast-food juggernaut his father, Truett Cathy (d. 2014), founded in 1967.","He grew up doing odd jobs in his father's restaurants, including scraping chewing gum from table bottoms with a butter knife.","Cathy became CEO in 2013, sparking nationwide protests when he made anti-same sex marriage remarks. His son, Andrew Cathy, took over as CEO in 2021.","His brother, Bubba Cathy, serves as executive vice president of the chicken chain, which is known for staying closed on Sundays."]
abouts: ["Cathy plays the trumpet and is an avid motorcyclist and licensed pilot.","Cathy spends his Sundays teaching Bible study to high school students."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Dan Friedkin owns Gulf States Toyota, which sold $13 billion worth of Toyotas in 2025.","The company, based in Houston, has exclusive rights to distribute Toyota vehicles in Texas, Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi and Oklahoma.","His father Thomas, who started the business in 1969, died in March 2017.","Through The Friedkin Group, he also owns luxury hospitality management firm Auberge Resorts, which has properties in Aspen and Cabo San Lucas.","NEON, his film studio, won four Academy Awards for \"Parasite\" in 2020, produced Martin Scorsese's 2023 drama \"Flowers Of The Killer Moon\" and won five Oscars in 2025 for \"Anora\".","In December 2024, The Friedkin Group acquired fellow billionaire Farhad Moshiri's majority stake in Everton Football Club, the English soccer team."]
abouts: ["His Friedkin Conservation Trust is working to preserve more than 6 million acres in Tanzania.\r\n","Friedkin owns one of the largest collections of vintage military war planes in the country."]
title: owner and ceo

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Dan Gertler built a fortune through mining ventures in Africa, primarily in the Democratic Republic of Congo.","In February 2017, he sold his stake in two mines in the Congo to commodities giant Glencore for $960 million; Gertler made an estimated $400 million.","In December 2017, the U.S. government placed Gertler on its sanctions list for his alleged corrupt business deals in the Congo. Sanctions have been eased in recent years.","In June 2018, the U.S. levied sanctions against 14 additional companies of his, including Fleurette Africa Resources and  Ventora Development Sasu.","A spokesman for Gertler declined to comment on the U.S. government's allegations."]
abouts: ["Gertler's grandfather, Moshe Schnitzer, cofounded the Israel Diamond Exchange in 1947.","He bought his first mine in the Democratic Republic of Congo in 1997 and soon became friends with DRC President Joseph Kabila."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Dan Kurzius founded what later became Mailchimp with Ben Chestnut in 2001 as a side project to their web design company.","Mailchimp's email marketing software for small businesses garnered enough customers that in 2007 they committed to it full time.","Wary of giving up control to outside investors, Kurzius and Chestnut bootstrapped growth from profits and took no outside money.","In 2021, Intuit announced it would acquire Mailchimp in a $12 billion cash and stock acquisition.","At the time of announcement, Chestnut and Kurzius each owned 50% of the Atlanta-based company, which had $800 million in 2020 revenue."]
abouts: ["Kurzius was a part-time DJ and competitive skateboarder before getting into web design.","The two cofounders met when Chestnut hired Kurzius to work at Cox Interactive Media's dot-com era MP3 music service."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Dan Sten Olsson is CEO and majority owner of Stena Sphere, a privately held Swedish conglomerate.","Interests include cruising, shipping, offshore drilling, property and metal recycling.","Stena was founded in 1939 as a trading company by Dan's father, Sten.","Dan took over in 1983 and now owns 51% of the company; his siblings Stefan Sten Olsson and Madeleine Olsson Eriksson own 24.5% and 12.5%, respectively","Madeleine's kids Gustav and Marie each own 6%  and have seats on different board in the firm."]
abouts: ["In 1946, the company founder Sten purchase his first vessel, a three-masted schooner named Dan. One year later his first son is born, and given the same name."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Dan Snyder initially made his fortune with a marketing business, Snyder Communications, that he started as a college dropout.","After taking the company public in 1996, Snyder sold it to French firm Havas for $2.1 billion in stock in 2000.","In 1999, he bought the NFL's Washington Commanders for $750 million, borrowing $350 million to do so. He sold the franchise for $6.05 billion in 2023.","After years of controversy over the Native American origins of the team's former name, the Redskins, Snyder renamed the team the Commanders in 2022.","In 2019, Snyder made waves with his new $192 million yacht Lady S, which has an IMAX theater.","Snyder cleaned and mopped the floors at the cafeteria inside the National Institute for Health as a high school student."]
abouts: ["In 1996, Snyder was the youngest public-company CEO on the New York Stock Exchange.","Snyder dropped out of college to start a business chartering planes to fly college kids to sporting events. By 20 he was a millionaire."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Dan and his brother Farris got a combined $3.5 billion (pretax) in 2011 selling their fracking company to a group led by Singapore-based firm Temasek.","The brothers have acquired more than 672,000 acres of land in six different states across the West, becoming America's 12th-largest landowners.","They first founded Wilks Masonry in 1995, following in their stone mason father's footsteps.","In 2002 they went into fracking, launching Frac Tech and growing it into an oil and natural gas giant before cashing out less than a decade later.","The brothers are also investing in oil and gas businesses, including fracking company U.S. Well Services and data provider Dawson Geophysical Company."]
abouts: ["Dan Wilks and his brother are active Republican donors.","The brothers reportedly spend four months a year in Montana, working on building homes on their  large ranches."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Dang Yanbao is the chairman of Ningxia Baofeng Energy Group, a supplier of coal chemical products.","He worked in building materials and investment before setting up Baofeng Energy in 2005.","Another private firm, Baofeng Energy Storage, began trial production at its 100GWh battery and energy-storage plant in northwestern China's Yinchuan city in 2024.","In 2025, Baofeng Energy began operations at a $6.7 billion olefins plant in Inner Mongolia, one of the world's largest, raising the company's annual capacity for olefin to 5.2 million tons."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Dan Calugar is a private investor based in Las Vegas, Nevada.","Calugar worked as a tax lawyer in Atlanta the late 1970s and 1980s before switching to investing in mutual funds.","He has invested using data-driven strategies across mutual funds, stocks, hedge funds, structured fixed income, volatility and managed futures.","He now primarily invests in an externally managed energy strategy and an in-house algorithmic stock trading program he developed internally.","In 2003, he settled alleged charges of fraud through improper late trading and market timing with the SEC for $225 million. He did not admit or deny the charges."]
abouts: ["Calugar attended the Air Force Academy and is a commercial pilot with more than 3,500 hours.","Calugar has flown over 200 Angel Flight missions, providing free air transport for passengers in need of medical treatment and for community service."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Daniel Chiu chairs Fortune Oil, a Hong Kong-based oil and gas supplier that also operates infrastructure projects in mainland China.","Through Fortune, Chiu also owns a large stake in China Gas Holdings, a Hong Kong-listed distributor of natural gas and operator of gas pipelines.\r\n","Chiu is the founder of the Harrow International Schools, which has 12 locations in Bangkok, Beijing, Hong Kong, Shanghai and Japan's Appi.","Also known as Chiu Tat Jung, he broke into the billionaire ranks in 2019."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Daniel D'Aniello is one of three billionaire founders of private equity firm Carlyle Group.","He stepped down as chairman in 2018 and now serves as chairman emeritus of Carlyle, which has $453 billion in assets under management.","D'Aniello worked at Trans World Airlines, Pepsi and Marriott before joining William Conway Jr. and David Rubenstein to start Carlyle in 1987.","He attended Syracuse University on a scholarship, studying transportation economics, and later got his MBA at Harvard.","A Vietnam War veteran, D'Aniello contributed $20 million to Syracuse University's National Veterans Resource Center in 2018.","He is the chairman of the Virginia-based performing arts nonprofit Wolf Trap Foundation where First Lady Jill Biden is the honorary chair."]
abouts: ["He worked 60 hours a week in the summers and 20 hours a week during school as a stock boy in a produce market from age 9 until graduation.","D'Aniello was on the gymnastics team at Syracuse University.","He was the only child of a single mother who worked four jobs simultaneously for 25 years to keep them above the poverty line."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Daniel Dines is cofounder and CEO of UiPath, a robotic process automation company that went public on the New York Stock Exchange in April 2021.","Dines started DeskOver in 2005 in Bucharest, Romania. He later renamed it UiPath and moved its headquarters to New York City in 2018.","Customers like Japan's Sumitomo Mitsui bank or Toyota North America can spend millions on UiPath's virtual \"robot\" that can automate complex, repetitive tasks.","An avid reader, Dines said in a 2019 Forbes cover story that he reads in the mornings, often not showing up to UiPath's office until 11 am.","UiPath recorded $1.4 billion in revenue and a net loss of $74 million in the fiscal year through January 2025."]
abouts: ["In October 2019, after a period of rapid hiring at UiPath, the company laid off more than 300 employees, or about 11% of its workforce."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Daniel Ek is the cofounder of streaming music service Spotify and remained its CEO through 2025. ","He announced plans to assume the role of executive chairman in 2026, focusing more on the company's long-term strategy. ","Ek and his business parter Martin Lorentzon founded the company in 2006 in Sweden, and launched the product in 2008.","Today, Spotify boasts over 696 million users and 276 million subscribers across 184 markets.","In September 2021, Ek pledged to invest 1 billion euros in European technology, cofounding VC firm Prima Materia","Ek is also a cofounder of Neko Health, a medical tech firm that specializes in preventative scans to promote early disease detection; in 2026, the Stockholm-based company raised $700 million at a $7 billion valuation.  "]
abouts: ["Ek plays guitar, bass, drums, piano and harmonica and is close friends with Facebook cofounder Mark Zuckerberg."]
bio: When Daniel Ek joined the inaugural Forbes Under 30 class in 2012, his music streaming experiment Spotify had 10 million active users, was worth $2 billion and had just entered the U.S. Today, Spotify, which recently had a market cap of $50 billion, streams 70 million songs to nearly 400 million users across 184 markets. Ek, who is personally worth more than $4 billion, is now moving Spotify past pop-stars and opening his super streamer to storytelling, live talk and a new breed of audio creators in a bid to own the world's digital eardrums.
title: CEO

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Daniel Feffer is one of four billionaire brothers who control of Suzano, a Brazilian pulp and paper firm founded in 1924 by their grandfather.","The second-eldest of the brothers, he is vice-chairman of Suzano, which in early 2019 acquired rival Brazilian pulp and paper firm Fibria.","An advocate of open markets, Daniel Feffer is the chairman of the Brazilian branch of the International Chamber of Commerce.","He also founded Intelligent Tech & Trade Initiative, a project exploring how new technologies such as AI and blockchain can improve international trade negotiations."]
abouts: ["Suzano is the world's largest producer of eucalyptus pulp."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Dan Gilbert cofounded what would become Rocket Mortgage, the second-largest mortgage lender in the U.S., in 1985 at 22 years old.","Gilbert took the firm public as Rocket Companies in August 2020. Rocket originated $101 billion in mortgages in 2024.","He owns the NBA's Cleveland Cavaliers.","He and his companies have committed more than $7 billion to acquiring and restoring more than 100 properties in downtown Detroit and Cleveland.","Gilbert also cofounded online sneaker sale platform StockX, which became a unicorn in June 2019."]
abouts: ["Gilbert started his mortgage lender, then named Rock Financial, with $5,000 earned from selling pizzas in college.","Gilbert sold Rock Financial to Intuit for $532 million in 1999. He bought the firm, then renamed Quicken Loans, back 3 years later for $64 million."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Daniel Hager is a major shareholder of Hager SE and serves as the Chairman of the Supervisory Board.","The company is a leading provider of solutions and services for electrical installations, covering business fields such as energy distribution, cable management, and building automation.","Hager SE generates consolidated group revenues exceeding $3.5 billion annually.","Originally founded as a GmbH, the company has a history spanning over three decades and transitioned into a Societas Europaea (SE) in May 2007.","The group operates internationally with a workforce exceeding 13,000 employees and manages well-known brands such as Hager, Berker, and E3/DC."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Daniel Hirschfeld is chairman of Nebraska-based casual clothing retailer The Buckle; he owns about a third of the company.","The Buckle has 440 stores in 42 U.S. states and sells clothing online as well.","Hirschfeld's grandfather opened a men's clothing store in the early 1900s and his dad started the current business in 1948.","Under Hirschfeld, the retailer turned its attention to denim and added women's clothing in the 1970s.","Hirschfeld stepped down as CEO in 1991, a year before the company went public."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Dan Hunt owns the NFL's Kansas City Chiefs with his three siblings. His brother Clark is chairman and CEO.","Their father Lamar Hunt (d. 2006) founded the team and passed control to his kids in 2005. Lamar is credited with naming the Super Bowl.","Forbes estimates the Chiefs are now worth more than $4.7 billion (net of debt). Each Hunt Sibling owns an estimated 25% stake.","The Hunt siblings also own MLS team FC Dallas and a minority stake in the NBA's Chicago Bulls. Clark is chairman and CEO of the family's soccer club, while Dan is president.","Lamar was one of 11 heirs of oil wildcatter H.L. Hunt (d. 1974) who appeared on the first ever Forbes 400 list of the richest Americans in 1982."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Daniel Kretinsky runs and owns Energeticky a prumyslovy holding (EPH), the biggest energy group in Central Europe.","EPH, which employs more than 25,000 people, distributes and supplies electricity as well as provides gas storage and transmission.","During the 2020 market crash, he took the stock market by storm making bets on companies like Macy's, Foot Locker, Sainsbury and Royal Mail.","Kretinsky also owns stakes in French newspaper Le Monde and German retail giant Metro AG."]
abouts: ["Kretinsky is co-owner of Sparta Prague, one of the biggest soccer clubs in the Czech Republic.","His girlfriend is 22-year-old Anna Kellnerova, the oldest daughter of Petr Kellner, the richest Czech and his partner in a few deals."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Daniel Loeb is the founder of Third Point, a New York-based hedge fund launched in 1995 that manages $20 billion.","Loeb is known for launching activist campaigns against corporate boards, shaking up companies in various industries and countries.","Despite briefly enlisting a co-chief investment officer in 2019, Loeb, who also serves as Third Point's CEO, reassumed the role of sole CIO in 2020.","The Margaret and Daniel Loeb Foundation supports Alzheimer's research, education reform and LGBT rights.","Third Point acquired credit investing firm Birch Grove in 2025 to expand its presence in collateralized loan obligations and private credit."]
abouts: ["Loeb helped launch an initiative designed to protect LGBT rights globally and serves on the board of Success Academy Charter Schools in New York."]
title: Founder

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Daniel Lubetzky founded snack bar company Kind Healthy Snacks in 2004 and sold the majority of it to candy and pet food giant Mars in 2020.","Mars initially bought a minority stake in Kind in 2017 for an undisclosed amount; the 2020 deal reportedly valued Kind at $5 billion.","Lubetzky retains a financial stake in Kind, the size of which is undisclosed. Kind is known for its bars made with nuts and other ingredients.","Prior to Kind, Lubetzky started PeaceWorks, a marketing, consulting and distribution company, in 1994.\r\n","PeaceWorks specialized in selling items produced by groups in conflict, such as chocolates from Arabs and Israelis.","While traveling for PeaceWorks, Lubetzky found a bar with whole nuts and fruit in Australia which became the impetus for Kind."]
abouts: ["While in high school and college, Lubetzky purchased watches wholesale and sold them at a markup at flea markets and shopping mall kiosks. \r\n","Lubetzky wrote a 268-page senior thesis at Trinity University about achieving peace between Arabs and Israelis through business ventures."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Daniel MacMillan is one of 21 billionaire heirs to Cargill, America's largest private company.","His great-great-grandfather, W.W. Cargill, founded the business as a single grain warehouse on the end of an Iowa railroad line in 1865.","The family still owns roughly 90% of Cargill, which did $154 billion in 2025 sales across food, agriculture, financial and industrial divisions.","He's one of nine billionaire siblings who inherited stakes in the company from their father John H.  MacMillan III, who died in 2008."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Daniel Mate is the former head of zinc at commodities giant Glencore.","Mate joined Marc Rich & Co. in 1988 in Switzerland, six years before the firm was bought out by management and changed its name to Glencore.","Mate rose to co-directing the zinc, copper and lead commodity department in 2000. He retired in July 2020."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Daniel Nadler cofounded OpenEvidence in 2022 to use AI to help doctors make sense of the voluminous amount of medical research.","OpenEvidence has reached a valuation of $12 billion after an early 2026 funding round. Nadler owns nearly 60% of the company.","Before founding OpenEvidence, Nadler cofounded Kensho, which used AI for financial intelligence. He sold that company to S&P for $550 million in 2018.","OpenEvidence has signed up more than 758,000 doctors, and is adding them at a rate of 55,000 per month. It's free for verified doctors, and makes its money from advertising."]
abouts: ["Nadler wrote his Harvard Ph.D. thesis on the pricing mechanisms of credit derivatives. He also studied poetry under Pulitzer Prize-winner Jorie Graham."]
bio: Daniel Nadler is cofounder and CEO of OpenEvidence.

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Dan Och founded Och-Ziff Capital Management, now a publicly traded hedge fund firm, in 1994.","Och stepped down as chairman in 2019 after years of client withdrawals and no longer has a role with the hedge fund.","The firm changed its name to Sculptor Capital Management in August 2019, further cutting its ties with its founder.","Och now runs his family office, Willoughby Capital, a growth equity investor with a portfolio that includes Robinhood, Coinbase and Instacart.","Och has given more than $500 million to his charitable foundation, according to available tax filings.","Och, a longtime New Yorker, switched his residency to Miami Beach, Florida in late 2019."]
title: Founder

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Daniel Pritzker is one of 13 billionaire heirs in the Chicago-based Pritzker family, whose best known creation is Hyatt Hotels.","A filmmaker, in 2019 Pritzker released Bolden, a biographical drama about New Orleans trumpeter Buddy Bolden, after over a decade working on it.","He made a silent film, Louis, about the life of Louis Armstrong, which was released to critical praise in 2010.","Daniel's brother Tom is the chairman of Hyatt Hotels; his sister Gigi is a film producer.","Daniel's charitable foundation, named after his father and Hyatt founder Jay Pritzker, pledged $100 million to California community colleges in 2020."]
abouts: ["Pritzker used to own Jerry Garcia's guitar; he auctioned it and donated the proceeds, $3.2 million, to the Southern Poverty Law Center.","Pritzker is also a guitarist and the primary songwriter for Sonia Dada, a fusion rock and soul band."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Daniel Rocher is the son of Yves Rocher, who founded the French cosmetics giant Groupe Rocher in 1959.","Groupe Rocher owns beauty and personal care brands such as Yves Rocher, Arbonne, and Dr. Pierre Ricaud, as well as the French clothing line Petit Bateau.","In 1980, Daniel founded the cosmetics company Daniel Jouvance, which incorporates marine-based ingredients into skincare products.","Along with his nephew Bris, Daniel is one of the largest shareholders of Groupe Rocher, which remains under family control; the company brought in approximately 2.4 billion euros in sales in 2022."]
abouts: ["Daniel Rocher is a sculptor and art collector; in 2019, he purchased a castle in the Provence region of France and transformed it into an open-air gallery."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Daniel Sundheim is chief investment officer of hedge fund D1 Capital Partners, which he founded in 2018.","The firm has around $31 billion in assets under management, with the majority invested in private companies, including a large SpaceX stake.","D1 Capital's public and private portfolios both returned more than 30% in 2025, reaching new highs to recover from losses in 2021 and 2022.","Sundheim graduated from the University of Pennsylvania and spent 15 years working under billionaire Andreas Halvorsen at Viking Global Investors."]
title: Investor
residenceMsa: New York-Jersey City-White Plains, NY-NJ Metropolitan Division

name: Billionaires
bios: ["With billionaire brother Richard, Daniel Tsai leads Fubon Financial Holding, a family company with interests in banking, insurance and securities.","The brothers are investors in Taiwan Mobile, a mobile phone service provider, and Momo, a TV-shopping and ecommerce business.","They also own a stake in Diamond Biofund, a Taipei-based biotech venture capital firm that went public in 2023.","Cousins Tsai Hong-tu, Tsai Cheng-da and T.Y. Tsai are also billionaires."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Daniel Ziff and brothers Robert and Dirk inherited a fortune that dates back to 1927 when their grandfather cofounded publishing company Ziff Davis.","Daniel's late father, William Jr., built up Ziff Davis, which became best known for such trade publications as PC Magazine and Car and Driver.","The publishing business was sold for $1.4 billion in 1994.","The brothers created Ziff Brothers Investments and greatly expanded their inheritance with hedge funds in the U.S. and in London.","Ziff Brothers Investments ceased operations in 2014; the brothers are reportedly investing with former employees of their hedge funds."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Daniela Amodei is cofounder and president of Anthropic, which builds large-scale artificial intelligence systems.","She cofounded Anthropic in 2021 with six other former OpenAI employees, including her brother Dario Amodei, who is CEO.","Anthropic, which private investors valued at $380 billion in February 2026, has partnerships with Google's parent company Alphabet and Amazon.","Amodei worked at OpenAI for about three years as an engineering manager and vice president.","Amodei studied English literature at the University of California, Santa Cruz, then joined fintech unicorn Stripe in 2013 as a founding recruiter."]
title: Cofounder & President

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Daniela Grogg is the daughter of Peter Grogg, founder of Swiss biochemical company Bachem Holding AG.","Peter Grogg, who died in 2025, started the business in 1971 and served as CEO until 2002, and chairman until 2012.","Grogg, along with her billionaire sister and mother, all serve on the board of the family's asset management firm Ingro Finanz AG.","Bachem AG develops and manufactures active pharmaceutical ingredients, including peptides, amino acid derivatives and other organic molecules.\r\n","The family controls about 58% of Bachem as well as shares in Swiss electrical engineering company Burkhalter Holding and chemical maker Dottikon.\r\n"]
abouts: ["In 1971, Grogg started Bachem with 50,000 Swiss Francs."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Danielle Bellon is the widow of Pierre Bellon, who founded food service and catering company Sodexo in 1966. \r\n","Pierre Bellon, who expanded Sodexo to 56 countries, died in 2022 at age 92.","Danielle and Pierre's daughter Sophie served as CEO of the Paris-listed business for four years until late 2025.\t","Their son, François-Xavier Bellon, is chairman of family holding company Bellon S.A.","Their daughter, Nathalie Bellon-Szabo, heads events hospitality arm Sodexo Live!"]
abouts: ["Sodexo has catered for a wide range of customers, feeding people everything from mining sites in Africa to six Olympic games since 1988.","According to a 2015 agreement, Pierre Bellon's four children and direct descendants cannot sell shares held in the family holding company until 2058."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Danilo Iervolino is an Italian entrepreneur who founded online university UniPegaso in 2006, one of the first to be established in Italy.","Iervolino started UniPegaso at age 28 and grew it to become the largest in Italy, serving more than 120,000 students.","He sold his company Multiversity, which includes UniPegaso, to private equity firm CVC Capital Partners for $1.3 billion in October 2021.","Since selling UniPegaso, Iervolino has purchased Italian soccer team Salernitana.","He also invests in Italian tech startups, both independently and through a startup accelerator and venture capital funds."]
abouts: ["Iervolino was inspired to launch an online university in Italy when he traveled to the U.S. after developing online master's programs at the University of Salerno."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Danna Azrieli is an heir to the Azrieli Group real estate fortune.","She and her two sisters, Naomi and Sharon Azrieli, own about 46% of the publicly traded company.","She inherited her stake after her father, David Azrieli, died in 2014.","Danna chairs Azrieli Group, which builds shopping malls and office buildings in Israel."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Dannine Avara and her three siblings inherited Enterprise Products Partners, the energy pipeline giant founded by their late father, Dan Duncan.","Formerly the richest person in Houston, Duncan died in 2010 at age 77 of a brain hemorrhage.","Duncan started Enterprise Products in 1968 with $10,000 and a truck; now it owns over 50,000 miles of natural gas, oil and petrochemical pipelines.","Avara's sister Randa Duncan Williams is the only sibling on the board of the company."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Danny Harris owns popular athleisure brand Alo Yoga with his childhood friend turned business partner, Marco DeGeorge.","The pair met while growing up in the San Francisco suburb of Los Gatos and began selling T-Shirts together after graduating high school.","In 1992, Harris and DeGeorge launched Color Image Apparel and found success screen printing apparel for wholesale.","They created the Alo Yoga brand in 2007, and nearly two decades later, its $118 leggings and $68 biker shorts have become a hit with celebrities and influencers.\r\n","Alo Yoga made up the vast majority of Color Image Apparel's nearly $2 billion of estimated revenue in 2024.","Alo has expanded to more than 150 brick-and-mortar stores worldwide, including 56 outside the U.S."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Darcie Glazer Kassewitz and her five siblings sold a quarter of their 68% stake in Manchester United to British chemicals billionaire Jim Ratcliffe in 2023.","The deal valued the team at $5.4 billion (net of debt). Their father, shopping mall magnate Malcolm Glazer (d. 2014), bought the team for $1.4 billion in 2005.","The Glazer siblings still own the NFL's Tampa Bay Buccaneers; their father acquired the franchise for $192 million in 1995, and it's now worth an estimated $5.2 billion (net of debt).","Darcie is chairman of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers Foundation and two other family charitable foundations.","Brother Kevin runs the family's real estate arm, Glazer Properties. Brothers Joel and Avram co-chair Man U. Joel also co-chairs the Bucs with brothers Bryan and Edward."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Dario Amodei is cofounder and CEO of Anthropic, which builds large-scale artificial intelligence systems.","He cofounded Anthropic in 2021 with six other former OpenAI employees, including his sister Daniela Amodei, who is president.","Anthropic, which private investors valued at $380 billion in February 2026, has partnerships with Google's parent company Alphabet and Amazon.","Amodei previously served as vice president of research at OpenAI, where he co-invented reinforcement learning from human feedback.","Amodei has a PhD in biophysics from Princeton University."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Poland's \"King of Shoes,\" Dariusz Milek created CCC, one of the biggest footwear retailers in Europe.","The CCC chain, which went public in 2004, has 980 shops in 23 countries.","In 2018, Miłek took over the number two shoe company in Switzerland and formed a joint venture with a German footwear retailer.","CCC also sells shoes online in 19 EU markets through eobuwie.pl.","Milek was a member of Poland's national youth cycling team and now owns CCC Cycling Group."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["Daryl Katz amassed a fortune in the pharmacy business, buying the Canadian rights to U.S. franchise Medicine Shoppe in 1991. \r\n","A few years later he snatched up struggling Canadian drugstore chain Rexall, then expanded to the U.S. market.","Katz, the son of a drug store owner,  has since sold off all of his pharmacy operations, pivoting his Katz Group to real estate and entertainment.","He has been co-developing a $2 billion, 25-acre complex in Edmonton's downtown that will include offices, condos and retail, among others.","Katz also owns his native city's NHL team, the Edmonton Oilers."]
abouts: ["Katz started off his career as a lawyer, then ran a chain of frozen yogurt stands after buying the Alberta franchise rights to Yogen Früz with other investors.","Katz is the majority owner of conservative news website LifeZette, founded by Fox News host Laura Ingraham."]
title: Founder and Chairman

name: Billionaires
bios: ["David Adelman is a real estate, alternative investments and sports mogul.","His Campus Apartments is one of the largest providers of on- and off-campus housing in America, with some $2 billion of properties across 80 schools in 23 states.","He is also cofounded Future Standard, an alternative investments firm that manages $86 billion across mutual funds, REITs and other vehicles. He's vice chairman.","He has a 7% stake in Harris Blitzer Sports & Entertainment, which owns the NHL's New Jersey Devils and the NBA's Philadelphia 76ers. He's spearheading a plan to build the Sixers a $1.3 billion arena.","A Philadelphia native, Adelman got his start using $2,000 of bar mitzvah money to invest with student housing entrepreneur and family friend Alan Horwitz.","He then went to work for Horwitz, rising to CEO at age 25, and began taking more and more of the equity as he expanded Campus Apartments nationwide."]
abouts: ["Adelman first invested in a building at the corner of 45th and Pine streets, which he still owns today. He chose it at age 13 because it was the tallest one he saw.","Through his Darco Capital, Adelman has invested in everything from soccer club Crystal Palace F.C. to private jet charter company WheelsUp, where he's on the board."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["David Baszucki is cofounder and CEO of Roblox, a social gaming platform that allows kids and teens to play games that are made by fellow gamers.","Roblox's 83 million daily active users spent more than 73 billion hours using the platform in 2024.","Players on the platform can buy a digital currency, Robux, which lets them purchase special items within games.","Robux purchases allow tween developers of games to earn money for their efforts. The company paid Roblox creators nearly $1 billion in 2024."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["David Blitzer runs the tactical opportunities group at alternative investment giant Blackstone. ","In 2011, he joined forces with then Apollo colleague Josh Harris to buy the NBA's Philadelphia 76ers. They later added the NHL's New Jersey Devils and English soccer club Crystal Palace to their holdings.","Blitzer also owns stakes in MLB's Cleveland Guardians, and he retained a minority stake in Real Salt Lake and the Utah Royals after the Miller Sports Group purchased a majority of the team in 2025.","Blitzer joined Harris' ownership group that purchased the NFL's Washington Commanders for $6.05 billion in 2023.","Blitzer graduated magna cum laude from the University of Pennsylvania's Wharton School."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["When David Booth cofounded Dimensional Fund Advisors in 1981, he began a decades-long experiment in applying academic theory to real-world investing.","His former professor Eugene Fama authored the efficient markets hypothesis, which argues that it's impossible to consistently beat the market.","In light of Fama's research, Booth eschewed stock picking and focused on offering investors low-cost, passive mutual funds.","Dimensional manages $777 billion in assets, most of which is steered via hand-vetted financial advisors.","Booth joined the Giving Pledge in 2018, committing to donate at least half of his wealth to charity."]
abouts: ["Booth paid $4.3 million for James Naismith's original rules of basketball, written in 1891, which is now displayed at the University of Kansas.","In 2008, Booth donated $300 million to the University of Chicago, which is still the largest gift in its history."]
title: Chairman and CEO

name: Billionaires
bios: ["David Chen is a cofounder of Singapore-headquartered online gaming and e-commerce firm Sea, best known for its hit mobile game, Free Fire.","He is the chief product officer of Shopee, the e-commerce unit of the NYSE-listed company. Previously he was Sea's chief operating officer and chief of staff.","Chen cofounded Sea in 2009 with Forrest Li and Gang Ye.","In 2023, Sea booked its first-ever annual net profit since its IPO in 2017.","Sea has rolled out digital banking services in Southeast Asia, Taiwan and Brazil."]
abouts: ["A computer engineer, Chen worked with Temasek-owned port operator PSA Corp before becoming an entrepreneur."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["\"Professor Billionaire\" David Cheriton, who is professor emeritus at Stanford University, made his fortune thanks to an early investment in Google.","Cheriton and Andreas von Bechtolsheim (also now a billionaire) each invested $100,000 in Google when it was just getting started.","The pair cofounded 3 companies: Arista Networks (IPO in 2014), Granite Systems (sold to Cisco in 1996) and Kealia (sold to Sun Microsystems in 2004).","Cheriton resigned from Arista's board in 2014.","Cheriton became chief data center scientist at Juniper Networks after the acquisition of his company Apstra in 2021."]
abouts: ["Cheriton, who is frugal in his personal life, is the third of six children of two Canadian engineers who grew up during the Great Depression.","Cheriton still lives in the Palo Alto home he's owned for 30 years and cuts his own hair."]
title: Professor

name: Billionaires
bios: ["David Dean Halbert became a billionaire in June 2025 when the diagnostics firm he built up, Caris Life Sciences, went public on the Nasdaq.","In 2008 Halbert acquired a small biotech firm called Molecular Profiling Institute, then greatly expanded it and renamed it Caris Life Sciences; he owns a 44% stake.","Caris Life Sciences uses gene sequencing, AI and machine learning for early disease detection; revenue at the unprofitable company grew to $412 million in 2024.","Halbert previously founded pharmacy benefit manager AdvancePCS in 1987. He took it public and later sold it to Caremark for $7.5 billion in 2004","He has been an active buyer and seller of healthcare businesses through his Caris Capital."]
bio: David Dean Halbert is founder, chairman and CEO of Caris Life Sciences.

name: Billionaires
bios: ["David Duffield cofounded not just one, but two successful enterprise software companies after age 40: PeopleSoft and Workday.","He resigned as chairman of Workday in 2021; he cofounded the HR and finance software firm in 2005 and took it public in 2012.","Duffield cofounded PeopleSoft at age 47 in 1987 and sold it to Oracle for $10.7 billion in cash in 2005.","He founded his sixth enterprise software company, Ridgeline, in 2017, and is chairman of the cloud software firm for investment managers.","He has spent more than $900 million supporting animal welfare, education and other causes, mostly via his family foundation and Maddie's Fund."]
abouts: ["Duffield mortgaged his home to bootstrap PeopleSoft in the 1990s.","Duffield says he plans to leave the bulk of his fortune to Maddie's Fund--named after his beloved schnauzer--and other charitable causes, not to his 10 children."]
title: Cofounder

name: Billionaires
bios: ["David Fattal founded Fattal Hotels, Israel's largest hotel organization.","Fattal got his start as a waiter and bellboy and rose through management ranks before starting Fattal Hotels in 1998 at age 41.","He took the chain's parent company, Fattal Holdings 1998, public on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange in 2018.","The company owns 47 hotels in Israel with 9,000 rooms, and manages 255 hotels with a total of more than 50,000 rooms across Israel, Europe and the Mediterranean region.","Fattal owns about 51% of Fattal Holdings and nearly 9% of Mediterranean Towers, which is also listed on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["David Feffer is the eldest son of Max Feffer, whose immigrant father Leon Feffer launched the family business.","His grandfather Leon Feffer founded Brazilian pulp and paper firm Suzano in 1924.","David and his three brothers - Daniel, Jorge and Ruben - each inherited shares in Suzano; David and Daniel are also board members of the company.","Suzano acquired Fibria in January 2019 for about $7.5 billion, creating Brazil's largest paper producer.","David is president of Suzano's board of directors and has headed the family's investment arm since 2003."]
abouts: ["Feffer began working for his family's company just before his eighteenth birthday.","He became the chief executive of Suzano in 2001, but later decided to step down and give the position to a non-family member."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["David Filo cofounded Yahoo, which sold its core business to Verizon for $5 billion in cash in 2016.","The most valuable part of Yahoo - its stakes in Alibaba and Yahoo Japan - morphed into a company called Altaba. Altaba voted to liquidate in 2019.","Filo and his wife Angela established the Yellow Chair Foundation in 2000; it supports education, civil liberties, gender equality and the environment.","In 2004, Filo donated $30 million to his alma mater, Tulane University, for engineering and computer science scholarships."]
abouts: ["Filo's wife Angela, a photographer and educator, sits on Stanford's Board of Trustees. David got a master's degree from Stanford in 1990.","Originally called \"Jerry and David's Guide to the World Wide Web,\" Yahoo was named after a word from Gulliver's Travels that meant \"rude, unsophisticated.\""]
title: Chief Yahoo

name: Billionaires
bios: ["David Fong is the managing director and co-chairman of Hip Shing Hong Group, one of Hong Kong's largest private real estate investment companies.","His late father Fong Yun Wah served as chairman of the group until 2022. His uncle is now co-chairman.","The family had an early sesame-seed-processing business, which eventually gave way to property investment and Hip Shing Hong started in 1948.","Today the group's businesses span across residential, commercial and hospitality.","David's son Jonathan is deputy managing director of the group; younger son Vincent runs his own business in healthtech."]
abouts: ["The company's roots date back to 1927, when Fong Yun Wah arrived in Hong Kong with his father from Guangdong province."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["David Geffen is the founder of record labels Asylum Records, Geffen Records and DGC Records, as well as film studio DreamWorks.","Born to Jewish immigrants in Brooklyn, Geffen started his career in the mailroom of talent agency William Morris, where he rose to become an agent.","Throughout the years he has amassed an impressive contemporary art collection, including works by Jasper Johns, De Kooning and Jackson Pollock.","A luxury property aficionado, he owns one of NYC's most expensive apartments, a house in the Hamptons and has owned two estates in Beverly Hills.","In 2017 Geffen pledged $150 million to the Los Angeles County Museum of Art, the largest gift in the museum's history."]
abouts: ["To keep his job in the William Morris mailroom Geffen lied about having graduated from college and created a fake UCLA degree. He admitted it once he was successful.","A storied bon vivant, Geffen owns one of the world's largest yachts, Rising Sun, whose guests often include Leonardo DiCaprio, Disney's Bob Iger and Oprah Winfrey."]
title: Cofounder

name: Billionaires
bios: ["David Golub is president of Golub Capital, a private credit firm with $75 billion in capital under management, and CEO of Golub Capital BDC.","After stints at Centre Partners and Corporate Partners, a fund affiliated with Lazard, Golub joined his brother Lawrence at Golub Capital in 2003.","Golub Capital specializes in lending to middle market companies backed by private equity sponsors and has offices throughout the U.S. and in London.","Golub is on the board of Burton Snowboards and supports numerous nonprofits, including the Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson's Research."]
abouts: ["After graduating from Harvard, David Golub was awarded a Marshall Scholarship and earned a masters in philosophy from Oxford University."]
title: President

name: Billionaires
bios: ["David Grain is the CEO of Grain Management, a private equity firm he founded in 2007.","Grain Management is focused on broadband and communication infrastructure investments.","Before founding Grain Management, he led wireless infrastructure company Global Signal from bankruptcy to IPO.","Grain Management purchased 15 megahertz of spectrum in T-Mobile's 800 MHz band in 2025 and Quintillion, an Alaskan fiber-optic network, in 2024.","Grain and his wife founded the Grain Fellows Program in 2004, funding SAT and college prep, application fees and mentorship for low-income students at Booker High School in Sarasota, Florida."]
abouts: ["He is a lifetime member of the Council on Foreign Relations.","Grain was appointed by President Barack Obama to the National Infrastructure Advisory Council at the U.S. Department of Homeland Security."]
bio: The son of a trucking entrepreneur, Grain was born in Brooklyn, earned a bachelor's from College of Holy Cross and an MBA from Dartmouth. Additionally, Grain held senior roles at AT&T and Morgan Stanley before founding private equity firm Grain Management in 2007. The firm invests in telecommunications infrastructure, including fiber networks, wireless spectrum and cellphone towers. Grain owns roughly 64 percent of the firm that's worth approximately $300 million. According to Forbes data, Grain is worth $1.1 billion.
title: Founder & CEO

name: Billionaires
bios:
["David Hindawi cofounded cybersecurity firm Tanium with his son Orion in 2007.
","Tanium has raised $800 million from investors who valued it at $6.5 billion in October 2018.","In February 2016, Orion took over as CEO from his father. David is executive chairman.","David, now a U.S. citizen, was born in Baghdad, grew up in Israel, and went to UC Berkeley for a Ph.D. in operations research.","He previously founded BigFix,an IT software patching system, with help from his son. They sold the company to IBM for $400 million in 2010.\r\n"]
title: Executive Chairman

name: Billionaires
bios: ["David Hoffmann owns 127 businesses, including everything from real estate developments to luxury transportation to executive search firm DHR International, the source of his early fortune.","Hoffmann bought the Pittsburgh Penguins for $1.75 billion in June, a price that NHL commissioner Gary Bettman described as low and a good deal.","Hoffmann is the majority shareholder of Lee Enterprises and sole shareholder of Hoffmann Media Group, which together own 154 newspapers and seven radio stations.","The self-made entrepreneur grew up in Washington, Missouri, where his dad drove a milk truck.  The family didn't have running hot water until he was in high school.","He and his wife Jerri, who moved to Naples in 2015, paid $105 million for a 24,202-square-foot estate with 12 bedrooms in the city's tony Port Royal neighborhood in 2025."]
abouts: ["Star quarterback Hoffmann got a football scholarship to Northeast Missouri State U. After an injury, he left school and later finished at U. of Central Missouri.","Hoffmann and his wife own four wineries and 1250 acres of vineyard in Missouri.","Hoffmann received the Horatio Alger Award in 2023, awarded to people who have overcome adversity to achieve professional and personal success."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["David Humphreys is an heir to the Galena, Kansas-based Tamko roofing fortune.","His grandfather E. L. Craig started the company in 1944 at the age of 69 in an old streetcar barn in Joplin, Missouri.","Today, Tamko is the fourth-largest manufacturer of roofing shingles in the United States. The company recorded $1.2 billion in 2023 revenue.","David took over as president and CEO of Tamko in 1994 after his father's death; he and his wife Debra both serve on Tamko's board of directors.","The Humphreys family sold a 25% stake in the business to the Carlyle Group, a $447 billion (assets under management) private equity firm, for an undisclosed sum in 2019.","David and his sister Sarah, and their respective families, split the remaining 75%."]
abouts: ["A libertarian who has given millions to Missouri Republicans, David Humphreys has also been an outspoken critic of President Donald Trump.","Humphreys' passions include tennis, rare books and history."]

name: Billionaires
bios: ["David Kabiller is a cofounder and head of business development at AQR, a quantitative investment firm with $187 billion in assets under management. ","AQR stands for Applied Quantitative Research. It focuses on factor-based investing, offering products ranging from hedge funds to mutual funds.","The firm is headquartered in Greenwich, Connecticut, with other locations in Bangaluru, Dubai, Hong Kong, London, Munich and Sydney.","Before AQR, he was a vice president at Goldman Sachs, working with chief investment officers of large pension and endowment funds in North America."]
abouts: ["Kabiller founded the Kabiller Prize and the Kabiller Young Investigator Award for researchers in nanoscience and nanomedicine at Northwestern University.","At Northwestern, his alma mater, Kabiller has founded a series of prizes and awards in the field of nanoscience and nanomedicine."]

name: Billionaires
